question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,2]\times [0,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-{y}^{3}+{x}^{2}y-3 \\ {x}^{3}y+{y}^{4}-4x+2\end{aligned}]. $$ Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts at ${x}_{0}=[1,\,0]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[1,\,2]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).
${x}_{1}≈[$ {{field-1}} $]$
$1.497$
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{4}-{y}^{3}+{x}^{2}y-3) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{4}-{y}^{3}+{x}^{2}y-3) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}y+{y}^{4}-4x+2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}y+{y}^{4}-4x+2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3}+2xy & -3{y}^{2}+{x}^{2} \\ 3{x}^{2}y-4 & {x}^{3}+4{y}^{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3}+2xy & -3{y}^{2}+{x}^{2} \\ 3{x}^{2}y-4 & {x}^{3}+4{y}^{3}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-{y}^{3}+{x}^{2}y-3 \\ {x}^{3}y+{y}^{4}-4x+2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3}+2xy & -3{y}^{2}+{x}^{2} \\ 3{x}^{2}y-4 & {x}^{3}+4{y}^{3}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-{y}^{3}+{x}^{2}y-3 \\ {x}^{3}y+{y}^{4}-4x+2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}. \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}4(1)^{3}+2(1)(2) & -3(2)^{2}+{1}^{2} \\ 3(1)^{2}(2)-4 & {1}^{3}+4(2)^{3}\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}{1}^{4}-{2}^{3}+(1)^{2}(2)-3 \\ (1)^{3}(2)+{2}^{4}-4(1)+2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}8 & -11 \\ 2 & 33\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 16\end{aligned}]. \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{8\cdot 33-(-11)\cdot 2}[\begin{aligned}33 & 11 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 16\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{286}[\begin{aligned}-88 \\ 144\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}1.308 \\ 1.497\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
